name: Retroformer: Retrospective Large Language Agents with Policy Gradient Optimization
authors: Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Juan Carlos Niebles, Zhiwei Liu, Yihao Feng, et al.; Salesforce AI Research
venue: ICLR 2024 (arXiv preprint Aug 2023, arXiv:2308.02151; DBLP conf/iclr/YaoHNLFXNC0AXMW24)
reflection_type: learned-critic-model (a small retrospective LLM is trained to generate verbal self-reflections that improve a frozen actor LLM)
feedback_source: environment-reward (episode returns / success rate from HotPotQA, AlfWorld, WebShop environments); the reward signal is the difference in episode returns between two consecutive trials, used to fine-tune the retrospective model
iteration_structure: episodic-retry-with-reset (agent retries the same task across N trials; reflections from failed trials are appended as long-term memory before each retry, and the retrospective model is fine-tuned offline from collected rollouts)
reflection_object: prompt/context plus model weights: the retrospective model edits the actor LLM's prompt (verbal reflection summarizing root cause of prior failed attempts + proposed action plan), and the retrospective model's own weights are updated by policy gradient. The frozen actor LLM's weights are never touched; learning is localized to the small retrospective model.
requires_training: RL (PPO via standard RLHF pipeline, trl/trlx framework, with LoRA fine-tuning of the retrospective model and KL regularization to a frozen reference model)
reward_or_critic_model: separate retrospective model trained with a reward defined from environment returns: the reward is the difference in episode returns between consecutive trials (credit-assignment-style shaping), optimized with PPO against the environment reward; the actor LLM is treated as part of the (frozen) environment
distillation_target: model-weights: the reflection-generation capability is distilled into the fine-tuned retrospective model's parameters (LoRA adapters on LongChat-7B-16k); per-task reflections themselves are still passed as prompt text to the actor
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered/scaffold-based reflection loop (Reflexion-style actor + reflection + memory architecture), but the quality of the reflective behavior is RL-optimized rather than purely prompt-engineered: the retrospective model is trained to produce better reflections, so reflection quality is learned via gradients
memory_type: long-term-episodic plus short-term/scratchpad, plus a replay buffer of (instruction, response, episode-return) tuples used for training
memory_persistence: cross-episode within a task (long-term memory of prior failed trials appended to the actor prompt) and cross-task (replay buffer aggregates good/bad reflections across tasks and environments for fine-tuning the retrospective model)
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only for the long-term reflection memory (reflections from failed trials appended to actor prompt); the training replay buffer is sampled (retrieval-gated by sampling) to fine-tune the retrospective model, providing demonstrations of good and bad reflections across tasks
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level (reflection summarizes the root cause of a failed trial / episode and assigns credit to actions affecting future rewards); operates at trajectory/episode level rather than token- or step-level
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both: intra-task refinement across retries of a single task via appended reflections, and inter-task transfer because the retrospective model is trained on a replay buffer spanning multiple tasks and environments and acts as a reusable plug-in
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only via episodic retry: the agent reflects after a failed trial and retries the task from reset in the next episode (it does not correct mid-trajectory in-flight)
task_domains: QA/reasoning (search-based question answering); embodied/games (text-based embodied robotics); web-navigation / decision-making (web shopping); tool-use (search/click action APIs)
benchmarks: HotPotQA (distractor dev, 100 validation tasks), AlfWorld (134 tasks), WebShop (100 tasks)
headline_result: Improves success rate over Reflexion baseline by +18% on HotPotQA (with 4 retries), +36% on AlfWorld (with 3 retries), and +4% on WebShop, using a frozen GPT-3/GPT-4 actor with a LongChat-7B retrospective model fine-tuned via policy gradient. With GPT-4 actor and LoRA r=4, Retroformer reaches 54% (HotPotQA, N=4), 100% (AlfWorld, N=4), and 46% (WebShop, N=4).
baselines: ReAct, Reflexion (frozen-LLM verbal reflection, Shinn et al. 2023), and SAC (a Soft Actor-Critic RL baseline); also positioned against Self-Refine and RAP in related work
gains_vs_baseline: vs the strongest comparable baseline Reflexion (N=4): HotPotQA GPT-3 50% -> 53-54%, GPT-4 52% -> 53-54%; AlfWorld GPT-3 84.33% -> 100%, GPT-4 85.07% -> 100%; WebShop GPT-3 35% -> 36%, GPT-4 44% -> 45-46%. The paper emphasizes faster learning (larger gains in the first few trials, e.g. +18% HotPotQA at trial 4, +36% AlfWorld at trial 3). Gains are largest on AlfWorld and smallest on WebShop (verbal feedback is suboptimal for the exploration-heavy WebShop environment).
compute_cost_profile: Inference: episodic retries (N up to 4) multiply rollout cost over a single pass, plus an extra retrospective-model forward pass per episode. Training cost is small and parameter-efficient: only the retrospective model is fine-tuned with LoRA (learnable params 0.53M for r=1, 2.25M for r=4) using offline RLHF/PPO; the large actor LLM (GPT-3/GPT-4) is frozen and requires no gradients, and gradients are not propagated through the actor.
known_limitations: Verbal-feedback reflection is suboptimal for exploration-heavy environments such as WebShop (only +4%), which require precise search queries and extensive exploration (also observed for Reflexion); gains on HotPotQA are modest (a few points); the approach still relies on environment reward signals and per-environment fine-tuning of the retrospective model; method tested only on three benchmarks with relatively small validation sets (100/134/100 tasks).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward: improvement relies on environment reward / task success signals (episode returns) to both append-trigger reflections and train the retrospective model; it does not depend on ground-truth answer labels at inference, but the retrospective model's training reward comes from environment returns (verifiable environment feedback rather than self-verification alone).
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (and environment/reward-dependent): training the retrospective model with environment reward yields consistent gains over frozen-LLM verbal reflection (Reflexion) across all three environments, with the benefit being task-dependent (large on AlfWorld, small on WebShop). Because correction is driven by external environment reward rather than intrinsic self-verification, it avoids the label-leakage critique while still being limited by reward informativeness.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; it focuses on success-rate gains)
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step (implicitly): the retrospective model is explicitly trained to perform credit assignment, summarizing the root cause of prior failed attempts and assigning credit of actions to future rewards, but it does not output a formal failure-mode taxonomy or per-step attribution scores
failure_mode_addressed: targets superficial/uninformative self-reflection (the motivating failure: a frozen LLM produces reflections that merely rephrase failed action sequences, causing repetitive incorrect actions and goal-forgetting over long interactions) and the credit-assignment problem in long multi-step trajectories; addresses error-loops/repetitive-action failures
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark dataset released; code and project page released (github.com/weirayao/Retroformer). Uses existing HotPotQA, AlfWorld, and WebShop; collects an internal replay buffer for training.
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); ReAct (Yao et al., 2023); RLHF / PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and the trl/trlx pipeline; LoRA (Hu et al., 2021); related verbal-refinement work Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023) and RAP (Hao et al., 2023); LongChat (longchat-7b-16k) as the base retrospective model
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited (~126 citations) by follow-ups on RL-trained reflection / verbal reinforcement and agent optimization, e.g. FinCon (synthesized LLM multi-agent with conceptual verbal reinforcement, 2024), GLoRe (when/where/how to improve LLM reasoning via global and local refinements, 2024), and self-reflective LLM stock-prediction work; surveyed in agent-memory and LLM-agent reflection surveys (e.g. A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of LLM-based Agents, 2024). Part of the lineage that distills/optimizes reflection signals rather than using frozen-LLM reflection.
reasoning_model_native: No: predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models; the actor is a non-reasoning frozen LLM (GPT-3 text-davinci-003 / GPT-4) and reflection ability is added via an external trained retrospective model rather than emerging from RL on the actor itself
on_policy_distillation_link: Related conceptually: distills reflection/credit-assignment skill into a small model's weights via offline policy-gradient (RLHF/PPO) on rollouts of the frozen actor; it is an early example of optimizing an auxiliary policy (the retrospective model) rather than the actor, conceptually adjacent to on-policy distillation / skill-optimization of a reusable reflection module, though training is offline from a replay buffer rather than strictly on-policy
sample_efficiency: Reported as a 'faster learner' than Reflexion: most of the gain appears in the first few retries (e.g. +18% on HotPotQA by trial 4, +36% on AlfWorld by trial 3); offline RL training data collected by rolling out the base policy for N trials per training task (exact rollout/gradient-step counts in Appendix C not fully specified here)
